Read-only audit. Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Be VERY thorough. Do NOT modify any file.

I need a precise inventory for SFCC-749 "Breadcrumb and SEO – PWA Kit Component": a breadcrumb on every page generated from page context, plus a collapsible SEO text block (title, intro, READ MORE / READ LESS expanding a body) rendered above the footer on category pages, content coming from Contentful keyed by category ID.

Investigate and report with EXACT absolute file paths:

BREADCRUMB:
1. Does an override exist at `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/`? Check both the working tree AND `git ls-tree develop overrides/app/components/`. Report definitively yes/no.
2. Read the BASE Salesforce component at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/breadcrumb/` (list files, read index.jsx fully). Report: the exported component, its props, what data shape it needs (categories array? shape of each item?), and whether it renders a Chakra Breadcrumb.
3. grep the WHOLE repo (overrides/ and node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/) for actual USAGE of the breadcrumb component — `from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/breadcrumb'` and `<Breadcrumb`. Report every call site: which page, what data it passes. Is it used on PLP? PDP? Anywhere in overrides/?
4. Is there a theme recipe for Breadcrumb? Check `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/` for a breadcrumb recipe.
5. PAGE CONTEXT / DATA AVAILABILITY — this is important: to generate a breadcrumb programmatically you need category hierarchy. Report what's available:
   - Read `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — what routes exist, what params do they carry?
   - Look at `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` — does it already have the category object (with `parentCategoryTree` or similar)? grep for `parentCategoryTree`, `useCategory`, `categoryId`.
   - Look at `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — does it have `primaryCategoryId` / category data for a PDP breadcrumb?
   - Check `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` (or jsx) for a categories context / `useCategories` / `CategoriesProvider`.
   - grep overrides/app/hooks/ for anything category-related.
   Be blunt: is the data needed for a site-wide breadcrumb already loaded on each page, or would it need new fetching?

SEO TEXT BLOCK:
6. Does anything resembling a collapsible "READ MORE / READ LESS" text block exist today? grep for `READ MORE`, `readMore`, `read_more`, `showMore`, `isExpanded`, `useDisclosure` across overrides/app/components/. Report candidates.
7. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmAccordion/` — read index.tsx and zimmAccordion.css.ts fully. Report full props, whether it's single/multi expand, whether it could serve a READ MORE/LESS pattern or is structurally an accordion only.
8. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductDescription/` — read it. Does it already implement expand/collapse of body text? This may be the closest existing thing.
9. `overrides/app/components/seo/` — does an override exist? What does it do (meta tags only, or structured data)? Check whether it emits JSON-LD BreadcrumbList structured data (important for SEO story). Also check the base at node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/.
10. Where would "above the footer" render? Read `overrides/app/components/pageContainer/` if it exists, and check how pages compose with the footer — is there a shared layout slot, or does each page render its own?

Report concisely with exact paths and blunt statements of what exists vs. what must be built. Explicitly flag every base-Salesforce file that would need the project's "copy-first" override treatment (copy from node_modules to overrides/, convert to TS, verify render, THEN modify) since that's a separate gated step.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation).      1	// SFCC-847 drawer/content/filters — accordion recipe. Tokens sourced from the Zimmermann
     2	// Design System 2026 Figma (node wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/40003890:151736 and /40003890:151742,
     3	// audited 2026-09-16). Divider colour resolves to `alias/color/border/secondary` in Figma
     4	// which binds to `#dddddd` — surfaced in this codebase as
     5	// `--zimm-color-border-tertiary` (see foundation/colour.ts `border.tertiary`). Figma's N+1
     6	// divider pattern (7 dividers for 6 accordions: top + between + bottom) is reproduced by
     7	// giving each item both `borderTop` and `borderBottom`, with no `_first`/`_last` override.
     8	
     9	export const ZimmAccordion = {
    10	  parts: ['root', 'item', 'header', 'label', 'alwaysVisible', 'panel'],
    11	  baseStyle: {
    12	    root: {
    13	      width: '100%',
    14	    },
    15	    // Every item carries both top and bottom borders so the accordion group reads as N+1
    16	    // dividers between headers, matching Figma. Chakra's own AccordionItem defaults are
    17	    // overridden here rather than layered on: the default `1px solid` uses the theme border
    18	    // colour, not the drawer-specific tertiary token.
    19	    item: {
    20	      borderTop: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-border-tertiary)',
    21	      borderBottom: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-border-tertiary)',
    22	      // Collapse the shared edge between adjacent items so a single 1px line renders instead
    23	      // of a doubled 2px seam. Only the last item keeps its own borderBottom.
    24	      _notLast: {
    25	        borderBottom: 'none',
    26	      },
    27	    },
    28	    // Chakra's AccordionButton is a real <button>; these sx overrides layer over its defaults
    29	    // (transparent bg, blackAlpha _hover, block layout). Cursor: pointer stays Chakra-owned.
    30	    // paddingBlock 20px per row yields ~41px between adjacent header baselines (20 + 1px
    31	    // border + 20), matching Figma's `Accordion group` gap-with-divider rhythm.
    32	    header: {
    33	      display: 'flex',
    34	      alignItems: 'center',
    35	      justifyContent: 'space-between',
    36	      width: '100%',
    37	      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)',
    38	      paddingInline: 0,
    39	      _hover: {
    40	        backgroundColor: 'transparent',
    41	      },
    42	      _focusVisible: {
    43	        // audit-allow: 2px matches Chakra's default focus-ring outline width; no dedicated
    44	        // Zimmermann token for outline width (only offset + composite).
    45	        outline: '2px solid var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
    46	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
    47	      },
    48	    },
    49	    label: {
    50	      // textTransform intentionally NOT set here — `textStyle="productNames"` (applied in
    51	      // index.tsx) already carries `textTransform: 'uppercase'` from the design system.
    52	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
    53	      flex: '1 0 0',
    54	      textAlign: 'left',
    55	    },
    56	    // Rendered directly below the header regardless of expanded state. Padding matches the
    57	    // panel's so a facet's chips align visually with the options list below when expanded.
    58	    alwaysVisible: {
    59	      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-s)',
    60	      paddingInline: 0,
    61	    },
    62	    panel: {
    63	      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-s)',
    64	      paddingInline: 0,
    65	      // Constrain children to available width. Without this, Stack/Flex children can expand
    66	      // beyond the drawer's bounds, causing horizontal overflow (audited 2026-09-16: Stack
    67	      // was 634px on 375px viewport). Width 100% + border-box ensures children don't exceed
    68	      // their parent's computed width.
    69	      width: '100%',
    70	      boxSizing: 'border-box',
    71	      overflow: 'hidden',
    72	    },
    73	  },
    74	};

    14	export type ZimmAccordionItem = {
    15	  /** Stable identifier — matches `defaultExpandedId` and acts as the React key. */
    16	  id: string;

    25	   * container — the real facet content (radio buttons, colour swatches, size chips, etc.)
    26	   * is SFCC-108's scope.
    27	   */
    28	  content: React.ReactNode;
    29	  /**

    31	   * use for a compact summary the shopper needs to see at a glance without expanding the
    32	   * accordion (e.g. the current selection chips for a filter facet). Hidden when the item
    33	   * is expanded so the full content in `content` takes over. Rendered outside Chakra's
    34	   * AccordionPanel, so it does not participate in the expand/collapse animation.
    35	   * Leave undefined for accordions with no summary.
    36	   */
    37	  alwaysVisibleContent?: React.ReactNode;
    38	};

    41	  items: readonly ZimmAccordionItem[];
    42	  /**
    43	   * Which item is open on first render. Uncontrolled — the user can toggle from here on
    44	   * without informing the parent.
    45	   */
    46	  defaultExpandedId?: string;
    47	};
    48	
    49	/**
    50	 * Single-open accordion group — a Zimmermann-styled wrapper around Chakra's Accordion
    51	 * primitive. Delivers SFCC-847's accordion behaviour: only one item expanded at a time
    52	 * (matches AC #5 and the DS 2026 Figma audited 2026-09-16, node
    53	 * wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/40003890:151742 which shows exactly one accordion expanded),
    54	 * expanding a new item collapses the previously expanded one, and each header exposes
    55	 * `aria-expanded` reflecting its state (unchanged from Chakra's own `AccordionButton`).
    56	 *
    57	 * The chevron swaps ChevronDown (collapsed) ↔ ChevronUp (expanded) using the render-prop
    58	 * form of `AccordionItem`. A CSS-only 180° rotation on a single glyph could animate

    60	 * 40002128:29217) are drawn as distinct shapes — swapping is faithful, rotating isn't.
    61	 *
    62	 * @param props see ZimmAccordionProps

    65	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_ACCORDION_RECIPE, {});
    66	  // `findIndex` returns -1 when the id isn't in `items`. Chakra's `defaultIndex={-1}` logs a

# PRD – Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL

*Last updated: 2026-06-11*

Scope: Magento→SFCC data migration, URL strategy and redirects, SEO (canonicals/hreflang, sitemaps/robots, rendering/headings/meta, structured data), and GEO routing foundations. Regional storefront routing, consent, and currency live in [regional.md](regional.md).

---

## 1. Data Migration (DMU-001 – DMU-012)

- Product feed via MuleSoft from AP21 to SFCC covering ~1,600 active SKUs: names, descriptions, attributes, imagery refs, category assignments (DMU-001). Ongoing product sync via MuleSoft post-migration. **DMU-002 — Confirmed (status flipped from Ready for Sign Off, 2026-06-11).** The PWA-side contract is settled: SFCC displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for product data (JT 04-06), with AP21 as the master of record. Upstream sourcing (the first load draws from **both AP21 and PLM** via MuleSoft, with Magento-enriched data migrated after the initial load) sits **outside the PWA boundary** — the PWA does not enrich or compute product attributes itself, it renders the MuleSoft payload. The earlier RJ challenges (PLM/Magento enrichment) are upstream-of-MuleSoft concerns, not PWA blockers.
- Multi-region catalogue assignments and regional merchandising preserved across all storefronts (DMU-003).
- Registered customer records (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-25): **only email address and Omneo ID** are migrated to SFCC. Name, phone number, saved delivery addresses, and communication preferences are sourced **live from Omneo at login**, not held in SFCC. The previously requested 20-address cap is no longer relevant (addresses are not stored in SFCC). FE must treat Omneo as the source of customer profile data post-login; degrade gracefully if Omneo is unreachable.
- **Customer passwords are not migrated** — customers must reset on first login (DMU-005). See AGENTS.md "Magento password migration" gotcha.
- Saved payment card details are **not** migrated; customers re-enter at next purchase (DMU-006).
- Historical order records are **not** migrated into SFCC. Order history is accessed via NewStore **through MuleSoft** where customer identifiers match across online and in-store channels (DMU-007, **Confirmed 2026-06-11** — status flipped from Ready for Sign Off). The PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for customer order history (JT 04-06); no order data is held in SFCC. ⚠️ Source-of-truth flag retained: the requirement text + JT name **NewStore via MuleSoft**, while an RJ comment says **"Order history will come from Omneo"** — the upstream source (NewStore vs Omneo behind MuleSoft) is out of the PWA boundary but remains unreconciled; see Open Items. For the ME storefront, only online orders appear in My Account order history; the orders API returns the most recent 50 orders held in NewStore, and until NewStore transitions in ME only online orders are visible — no FE customisation required to filter retail orders (DMU-008, Ready for Sign Off 2026-05-25).
- Contentful API connections reconfigured to point at the new platform; no bulk content re-entry needed (DMU-009, **challenged → Open** — RJ: no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful; reconciliation pending). Mechanism note: Contentful integrates as the headless CMS via the **Salesforce App Exchange connector**, consuming content through the Contentful **delivery API** for all customer-facing pages across all storefronts (Third Party Integrations: CMS / Contentful) — i.e. the integration is the App Exchange connector, not a bespoke API rewire.
- Product images and digital assets (DMU-010, de-scoped 2026-05-25): **out of scope for migration.** Images and assets are stored and served from Contentful — there is no CDN migration, no asset URL rewrite, and no 301 redirects for asset URLs. The existing Contentful API connection is simply reconfigured to point at the new SFCC platform as part of go-live (covered by DMU-009). (Source note records the **new** platform CDN as **Akamai** (SFCC default), whereas the **current** setup is **Cloudflare** (DMU-020). These are not in conflict — they describe current vs new platform CDN — but the migration must carry existing Cloudflare redirect/SEO rules forward to Akamai; see §2 DMU-019/DMU-020. No asset-migration impact, as assets stay in Contentful.)
- Migration approach: initial bulk export + one or more timestamp-based delta migrations + a final delta close to DNS cutover (DMU-011). Migration scripts must be repeatable and capable of multiple delta runs — one-off scripts are not acceptable (DMU-012).
- **Wishlist migration (Confirmed):** customer wishlist data migrated from Magento, wishlist items mapped to corresponding SFCC product records and associated to the migrated account via Omneo ID. FE renders the migrated wishlist post-login.
- **Product enrichment migration (Confirmed):** badges, category assignments, colour swatches, colour grouping, swatch images, and Shop the Look associations migrated from Magento to SFCC, mapped to the corresponding product/catalogue structure (Shop the Look display logic TBD).
- **Notify Me migration (Confirmed):** active Notify Me (back-in-stock) subscriptions migrated from Magento — customer email addresses and product IDs carried forward and mapped to SFCC product records.

---

## 2. URL Strategy (DMU-013 – DMU-020)

- Existing storefront locale prefix conventions preserved (DMU-013) — see [regional.md](regional.md) Section 1.
- AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — AU root stays globally crawlable; the bot allowlist in REG-009 exempts search engines and social unfurlers from the human geo-redirect, so `x-default` continues to point at the AU root).
- Existing product URL `.html` suffix preserved to maintain indexed URLs and avoid unnecessary 301 overhead (DMU-015).
- Category URLs updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`); 301s applied from all legacy category paths (DMU-014).
- 301 permanent redirects implemented for all URLs that change as a result of migration — products, categories, content, assets (DMU-017).
- All redirects implemented per the redirect mapping document, produced during build phase and validated pre go-live (DMU-018, **Open** — Accenture to propose redirect ownership; Zimmermann IT to review existing CDN rules).
- All 301s managed at CDN/edge level to minimise application-layer impact (DMU-019, **Open** — existing CDN redirect and SEO rules must be identified and carried forward, not auto-transferred).
- Existing CDN redirect rules and SEO configuration from the current Cloudflare setup preserved and carried forward to the new platform CDN (DMU-020).

---

## 3. SEO (DMU-021 – DMU-041)

### Canonicals & hreflang
- Canonical tags output on all indexable pages, referencing the preferred URL for the storefront (DMU-021).
- Filtered and faceted PLP URLs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP URL to prevent duplicate-content indexation (DMU-022, **Open** — Zimmermann wants the ability to override the canonical on selected indexable filter pages).
- hreflang tags applied only on canonical PDP URLs; non-canonical PDP variants do not carry hreflang but **do** retain canonical tags (DMU-023).
- hreflang implemented via XML sitemap format, mapping all locale codes to their respective storefront URLs (DMU-024).
- hreflang tags consolidated from the current 200+ country-specific tags to ~12 regional/language-level tags (DMU-025) — final structure to be confirmed with the Sparro SEO team prior to implementation.

### Sitemaps & robots
- XML sitemaps auto-generated per storefront and locale, refreshed daily (DMU-026). Disabled and deleted pages excluded on regeneration (DMU-027). Homepage URLs include trailing slash (DMU-028). URLs blocked in `robots.txt` must not appear in any sitemap (DMU-029).
- `robots.txt` permits crawling of indexable pages including the bag page; restricts checkout flow, account pages, search results, and filtered URL parameters (DMU-036).

### Rendering, headings & meta
- All product, category, and content pages rendered **server-side (SSR)** for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS (DMU-030).
- Title tags per page in the format `[Product Name] [Colour] | Zimmermann` — the legacy "Online" token has been removed as it consumes character space without value. Configurable via BM meta tag rules (DMU-031, updated 2026-05-15).
- Unique meta description tags per product and category page, sourced from product and catalogue data in SFCC. ## SEO TEXT BLOCK

### 6. READ MORE / READ LESS — **does not exist, at all**

Grep across `overrides/app/` for `read more|readmore|read_more|showMore|show more|readLess|read less|seeMore|viewMore` returns only:
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/static/adyen.css:40` — vendor class `.adyen-checkout-ctp__otp-readmore-button`. Irrelevant.
- `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/*.json` — base SFCC `store_locator.action.viewMore` in ~18 locales. Irrelevant.

No component, hook, or recipe. Chakra `Collapse`: **zero uses**. `noOfLines` / `lineClamp`: **zero uses**. Existing expand machinery in `overrides/app/components/` is only `useDisclosure` at `_app/index.tsx:195` and `header/rightBar/index.tsx:219` (both modal/drawer), plus `isExpanded` inside `zimmAccordion/index.tsx:76,82,88`.

### 7. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmAccordion/`

Files: `index.tsx`, `zimmAccordion.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`.

- **Named export `ZimmAccordion`** (no default). Props: `items: readonly ZimmAccordionItem[]`, `defaultExpandedId?: string`.
- `ZimmAccordionItem = { id: string; label: string; content: React.ReactNode; alwaysVisibleContent?: React.ReactNode }`.
- **Single-expand:** `<Accordion allowToggle defaultIndex={…}>` — `allowToggle` with no `allowMultiple`, so exactly one open, closable. **Uncontrolled** — no `onChange`, no controlled `index`.
- Recipe parts `['root','item','header','label','alwaysVisible','panel']`; every item carries `borderTop` + `borderBottom` (N+1 divider pattern), `paddingBlock: var(--zimm-scale-l)`, chevron swap Up/Down at `--zimm-icon-size-xl`.

**Verdict: structurally an accordion only — not usable for READ MORE/LESS.** The trigger `label` is a static string with no access to `isExpanded` (that render-prop is closed over inside the component), so you cannot swap "READ MORE" → "READ LESS". The chevron is hardcoded and non-removable. Full-width dividers are baked into `item`. `alwaysVisibleContent` hides on expand — it is a summary slot, not a truncated first-N-lines of the same body. Useful as a recipe/`useMultiStyleConfig` reference, nothing more.

### 8. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductDescription/`

Files: `index.tsx` (29 lines), `zimmProductDescription.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`.

- Named export `ZimmProductDescription`. One prop: `description?: string`.
- Body: `useStyleConfig('ZimmProductDescription')` → `if (isBlankRichText(description)) return null` → `parseRichText(description)` → `<chakra.div data-testid="product-description">`.

**It does NOT implement expand/collapse. No state whatsoever.** It is a pure rich-text renderer. It is *not* the closest existing thing to the collapse behaviour — it's only the closest for the *body rendering* half.

The genuinely reusable asset is `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` — `parseRichText` (`:115`), `richTextToPlainText` (`:240`), `isBlankRichText` (`:252`), `decodeEntities` (`:94`). Its docblock records a hard constraint worth carrying forward: **do not reintroduce `isomorphic-dompurify`** — it crashes SSR at import time (jsdom `__dirname` rewrite → ENOENT), reproduced 2026-08-23, was the flaw in PR #57.

⚠️ **Format mismatch:** `parseRichText` parses *SFCC Business-Manager HTML strings*. Contentful returns a **Rich Text document** (`ContentfulRichText` at `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:23`). `parseRichText` will not handle it. There is no Contentful rich-text renderer in the repo — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx:60-84` hand-walks `ContentfulRichTextNode` for exactly this reason. `@contentful/rich-text-react-renderer` is **not** a dependency (`package.json:129-130` has only `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` and `@contentful/live-preview`) — adding it trips AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 (integration-team approval).

### 9. `overrides/app/components/seo/` — **does not exist**

Not in the working tree, not on `develop`, and a scan of local branches found it on none.

- **Base:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/index.jsx`, 35 lines, `default Seo`, props `{title, description, noIndex, keywords, children, ...props}`. Renders a `react-helmet` `<Helmet>` with `<title>`, `meta[description]`, `meta[robots=noindex]`, `meta[keywords]`, then `{children}`.
- **Meta tags only. No structured data.** Grep for `application/ld+json|jsonld|json-ld|structuredData|schema.org|BreadcrumbList` across **both** `overrides/app/` **and** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` → **zero hits**. Nothing in this codebase emits JSON-LD.
- Also zero hits for `rel="canonical"` in either tree, despite DMU-021.
- **Call sites in overrides:** `_app/index.tsx:411` (site-wide: theme-color, apple-touch-icon, manifest, hreflang alternates), `pages/home/index.tsx:55`, `pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:347`, `pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx:149,161,172`, `pages/categoryPath/index.tsx:74`, `components/contentful/experienceBySlug/index.tsx:64,78,148,164`.
- **PLP and PDP do not use `<Seo>`** — each has its own inline `<Helmet>`: `product-list/index.tsx:1250-1257` and `product-detail/index.tsx:1109-1118`. So BreadcrumbList JSON-LD can land in those existing Helmets **without touching Tier 2 `seo/` at all**.

### 10. "Above the footer" — there is **no shared layout slot**

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` is the only layout. `<Box as="main" id="app-main">` wraps `{children}` (`:493-505`); `<Island hydrateOn={'visible'}>{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}</Island>` is a **sibling** at `:508`, immediately after `</SkipNavContent>`. **Nothing sits between them.**

So "above the footer" is either (a) the last child of each page's own tree inside `#app-main`, or (b) a **new slot inserted at `_app/index.tsx:507`** — a Tier 2 file.

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/pageContainer/index.tsx` is a 43-line width wrapper only (`boxed?: boolean | 'desktop'` → `maxWidth: container.xxxl` + responsive `paddingX`). **No slots, not a layout shell.** Used only by the PDP (`product-detail/index.tsx:1133, 1363`).
- `#app-main` is styled globally by `zimmAppMain` in `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts:236-247` (registered `:350`). PLP/PDP opt out with a negative `marginX` (`APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX`); a full-bleed SEO band would need the same technique.
- **Best PLP insertion point:** `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`, immediately after the `<Island><RecommendedProducts …/></Island>` block at `~:1492-1499` and before the sort `<Drawer>` / `<ZimmDrawer>` (both portalled, render nowhere in flow). That matches `.docs/prd/plp.md:18` ("below YMAL / Recently Viewed").
- Reminder: both `/search` and `/:segments+` render the *same* `ProductList` component. A category-gated SEO block must key off the `categoryId` **prop**, not the route.

**Contentful plumbing that exists:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — `useContentfulEntries<T>(contentType, preview, locale, filter, enabled, include)`. The `filter` arg takes raw Contentful search syntax, so `fields.categoryId=clothing-dresses` works directly, and `enabled` lets you skip on `/search`. **Closest pattern to copy: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts`** (builds a `fields.key[in]=` filter, fixed `CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE`, `enabled` gate, region scoping via `pickMostSpecificByRegion` from `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts` — a multi-storefront SEO block almost certainly needs that too).

⚠️ **Biggest technical risk in the story:** `useContentful.ts` is plain `useState` + `useEffect` + `fetch` — **not React Query**. It is **client-only: no SSR, no cache**. A Contentful-backed SEO block fetched this way **will not be in the server-rendered HTML**, which directly conflicts with DMU-035's whole purpose and with DMU-030 ("All product, category, and content pages rendered server-side for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS").
